title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ALGORITHMS IN MODELING ECONOMIC PROCESSES IN TOURISM
description: Tourism is one of the most dynamic sectors of the economy, but its key indicators — tourist flows, hotel occupancy, prices and revenues — depend on seasonality, prices, exchange rates and sudden external shocks. Traditional econometric models describe such processes only partly. This article examines the use of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms for modeling economic processes in tourism. A five-stage framework is proposed: data collection, data preparation, AI modeling, model evaluation and decision support, with a feedback loop for regular retraining. The main tasks solved by AI in tourism are classified: demand forecasting, tourist segmentation, dynamic pricing and recommendation. A computational experiment on a synthetic monthly series of tourist arrivals with trend, seasonality and a crisis shock compares a seasonal naive method, linear regression, random forest, gradient boosting and a neural network. Gradient boosting gave the lowest forecast error (MAPE 4.3 %), while the regression model gave 6.6 % and the naive method 14.9 %. The results show that AI algorithms can improve the accuracy of planning in the tourism sector when combined with well-prepared data and correct evaluation. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23576211

title: Algerian seawater desalination model: code, inputs and outputs. Supplementary Material 2 of "Can seawater desalination deliver 60% of Algeria's drinking water by 2030? A probabilistic techno-economic and brine-discharge assessment"

title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF PROVERBS IN ENGLISH AND UZBEK: LINGUOCULTURAL AND SEMANTIC PERSPECTIVES
description: This article compares English and Uzbek proverbs from semantic and linguocultural perspectives. It shows that many proverbs in the two languages express the same universal ideas about work, knowledge, friendship, patience and caution, but encode them through different images rooted in each nation's history, economy, religion and daily life. The study classifies proverb pairs into full, partial and zero equivalents and identifies culture-specific values: the central role of family, elders, hospitality and community in Uzbek proverbs, and of individual responsibility, time and pragmatism in English ones. Structural and stylistic features such as rhyme, parallelism and ellipsis are also compared. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23238699

title: CONTEMPORARY TRANSFORMATION OF THE PRODUCT LIFE CYCLE (IN TEXTILE PRODUCTS)
description: This article examines how digitalization, fast and ultra-fast fashion, and circular-economy regulation are reshaping the conventional product life cycle (PLC) in the textile and apparel industry. The study combines conceptual synthesis with secondary-data analysis from academic literature, the European Environment Agency, the European Commission, the Ellen MacArthur Foundation, McKinsey & Company, and the National Statistics Committee of Uzbekistan. The analysis distinguishes between the commercial life of a fashion item, which is becoming shorter and more data-driven, and the material life of textile products, which policy and circular business models seek to extend through durability, reuse, repair, resale, and fibre-to-fibre recycling. Evidence from Europe and Uzbekistan is used to show that competitive PLC management increasingly depends on rapid market sensing, flexible production, demand forecasting, circular design, and traceability. The paper proposes a dual-loop PLC framework and practical priorities for Uzbek textile enterprises seeking to move from cost-based competition toward higher-value, responsive, and sustainable export models. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23236893

It enables a structured and transparent assessment of financial viability by modelling revenue streams, capital and operating expenditures (CapEX, OpEx) as well as financing costs in detail. title: Code and data for "Vertical reach and life-cycle process exposures of marine heatwaves and cold spells in the East Sea" — surface-anchored vertical-reach census and life-cycle heat-transport diagnostics of East/Japan Sea MHW and MCS objects, 1993–2022

title: Coin-Based Reward Systems and Game-Driven Progression for Raising Educational Outcomes in Private Learning Centers
description: Private learning centers operate in a highly competitive market where learner retention, attendance and measurable progress determine institutional success. This paper proposes an integrated framework that combines a virtual coin economy with game-based level progression to increase learner motivation and academic performance in such centers. Drawing on self-determination theory, operant conditioning, flow theory and the gamification literature, the framework defines how coins should be earned, spent and capped; how levels, badges and quests should be structured; and how both mechanisms can be aligned with learning objectives rather than with participation alone. Implementation guidelines, risks (including the overjustification effect) and an evaluation plan based on a quasi-experimental design are presented. The paper is conceptual: it offers a practical, theory-grounded model that center managers and researchers can adopt and test empirically. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23610005

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND THE COMPETITIVENESS OF SMALL AND MEDIUM-SIZED ENTERPRISES IN UZBEKISTAN: CHALLENGES, OPPORTUNITIES AND STRATEGIC PRIORITIES
description: Digital transformation has become one of the most important drivers of economic growth, business competitiveness and structural modernization in developing economies. In Uzbekistan, the rapid expansion of digital infrastructure, electronic government services, financial technologies, e-commerce and innovative business models has created new opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). At the same time, insufficient digital skills, limited financial resources, technological disparities and inadequate managerial competencies continue to constrain the effective adoption of digital technologies by businesses. This article examines the role of digital transformation in increasing the competitiveness of SMEs in Uzbekistan. The study analyzes the main economic benefits of digitalization, identifies existing barriers to technology adoption, and proposes strategic priorities for improving the digital competitiveness of enterprises. Particular attention is paid to digital skills, access to finance, e-commerce, artificial intelligence, data-driven management and institutional support. The study concludes that the competitiveness of SMEs can be significantly strengthened through an integrated policy combining digital infrastructure development, human capital formation, financial incentives and modern business management practices. title: DIVERSIFICATION OF UZBEKISTAN'S EXPORTS AND INTEGRATION INTO GLOBAL VALUE CHAINS
description: Export growth in Uzbekistan since 2017 has been rapid, but it is unclear whether it reflects broader diversification or deeper participation in global value chains (GVCs). This article triangulates publicly available evidence for 2017–2026 to separate three questions: how concentrated Uzbekistan’s exports are by product and market, whether the composition of exports has shifted towards processed and capital goods, and what is known about domestic value creation within GVCs. Using World Bank WITS indicators (2017–2023), official Statistics data for 2024, 2025 and January–June 2026, and published GVC evidence for 2015, the analysis finds that the number of exported HS6 products rose by about 68% between 2017 and 2023, the raw-material share of goods exports fell from 12.1% to 5.7%, and capital goods rose from 1.7% to 6.3%. Market concentration, however, shows no trend (HHI between 0.11 and 0.29), and non-monetary gold remained about 28–29% of total exports in 2024–2025 before falling to 9.5% in January–June 2026 following a halt in gold sales rather than any structural change. Comparable post-2018 domestic value-added data could not be verified, so GVC deepening cannot be established; the article states this limit explicitly. Policy implications focus on measurement, firm-level upgrading, logistics and trade agreements, and are presented as hypotheses for further testing rather than causal findings. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23298979

title: Data and code: how much are America's forests worth? Farms, forests and fishing compared on value added, carbon, trade and research funding, United States, 1961 to 2025
description: Data, R and Python scripts, and figures behind an article for The Conversation US on crowded U.S. forests and the value GDP does not count, and its companion figure. The package compiles (1) gross and net value added (BEA GDP by Industry and Fixed Assets) for farms plus food manufacturing, wood plus paper manufacturing, and marine living resources (BEA Marine Economy Satellite Account), with each sector's own carbon priced at $51, $120 and $190 per t CO2e; (2) a forest ecosystem tally for 2022 that adds carbon taken up, clean air from all U.S. trees (Cavender-Bares et al. 2022), national forest water (Sedell et al. 2000) and national forest recreation (USDA Forest Service) to wood and paper value added, and charges agriculture FAO SOFA 2023 land, nitrogen and water damage; (3) export to import ratios for agriculture, forest products and seafood from UN Comtrade, 1981 to 2025, and FAOSTAT forest trade from 1961; (4) the EPA forest carbon sink and farm emissions, 1990 to 2023, and NOAA commercial landings with an estimated fleet carbon total; and (5) federal research capacity funds. Carbon is valued at estimates that a 2025 executive order withdrew from federal use. Dashed carbon lines in the current figure extend 1990 to 2023 linear trends to 2040 and are not forecasts. No Forest Inventory and Analysis plot data, coordinates or proprietary inventories are used. Version 1.1.0 adds the October 2026 four panel public figure (forests, farms and seafood in every panel), the sink, research fund and seafood hidden cost tables, and a third author. title: Data for "Future biodiversity risks of land-sourced aggregate mining"
description: This dataset contains model outputs and figure source data for a global assessment of construction-aggregate extraction, mining-area expansion and biodiversity exposure. global extraction.zip contains annual sand, gravel and limestone extraction for 142 economies from 2023 to 2050 under business-as-usual (BAU) and circular-economy (CE) scenarios. title: Datasets of Integrated Flood Risks of China under 1.5°C and 2°C Global Warming
description: This dataset provides spatially explicit integrated flood risk levels in China under global warming of 1.5°C and 2.0°C above pre-industrial levels for RCP8.5 scenario. title: ECONOMETRIC ASSESSMENT OF THE IMPACT OF PRODUCTION FACTORS ON IMPROVING THE ECONOMIC EFFICIENCY OF FOOD INDUSTRY ENTERPRISES
description: Abstract: In the context of increasing market competition, fluctuating input prices, and growing demand for high-quality food products, identifying the influence of these factors on enterprise performance has become an important research priority. This article examines the application of econometric methods to assess the impact of production factors on improving the economic efficiency of food industry enterprises. Particular attention is given to the relationships between labor productivity, capital investment, material costs, energy consumption, production capacity utilization, and financial performance. Correlation and regression analysis are considered as methodological instruments for identifying the statistical relationships between production inputs and economic outcomes. The study also discusses the importance of model specification, statistical diagnostics, and reliable data in obtaining valid econometric estimates. The proposed methodological approach can support the identification of major efficiency determinants, the optimization of production resources, the reduction of operating costs, and the improvement of managerial decision-making. The research provides a theoretical and methodological basis for further empirical studies aimed at strengthening the competitiveness and sustainable development of food industry enterprises. title: EMPLOYEE MOTIVATION AND HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT AS KEY DRIVERS OF SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS GROWTH
description: Employee motivation and human resource development are essential factors that influencing organizational performance, economic growth, and long-term business sustainability. In an increasingly competitive business environment, organizations should develop effective strategies to improve employee productivity, strengthen workforce capabilities, and promote sustainable management practices. The article gives information about the relationship between employee motivation, leadership effectiveness, training and development, and sustainable economic growth through a review of seven academic studies published between 2019 and 2025. The study shows a qualitative literature review approach to synthesize findings from research conducted in different organizational and geographical contexts, including Indonesia, Ukraine, Cambodia, and Nigeria. The reviewed literature indicates that employee motivation contributes to organizational sustainability by encouraging workforce engagement, enhancing productivity, supporting innovation, and improving organizational adaptability. title: ENDOGENOUS GROWTH THEORY AND ITS INFLUENCE ON CAPITAL ACCUMULATION
description: This article examines how endogenous growth theory explains the relationship between capital accumulation and sustained economic growth. It focuses on the roles of physical capital, human capital, knowledge, and research and development in expanding productive capacity. Particular attention is given to the mechanisms through which learning, innovation, and knowledge spillovers can affect investment incentives and returns to capital. The discussion distinguishes the accumulation of tangible assets from the development of capabilities that support their productive use. It also considers how institutional conditions, resource allocation, and public policy may influence these processes. The article aims to develop a conceptual framework for understanding the interaction between capital accumulation and technological change while recognizing differences among endogenous growth models and the conditions underlying their predictions. title: Egypt Census Village Deprivation Dataset
description: This dataset contains village-level deprivation indicators derived from Egypt's 2017 Population and Housing Census. It covers 4,702 rural villages across 24 governorates in Egypt and represents the complete rural settlement system included in the study, rather than a sample. The dataset was developed to examine multidimensional deprivation patterns and identify potential deprivation traps in Egypt's rural settlement system. It includes nine binary deprivation indicators covering housing conditions, infrastructure, education, gender and livelihoods. These indicators are used in an energy landscape analysis based on a pairwise maximum-entropy model to identify stable deprivation states, barriers between states and potential policy leverage points. title: FROM ECONOMIC INTERDEPENDENCE TO STRATEGIC RESILIENCE: RETHINKING LONG-TERM DEVELOPMENT IN THE GLOBAL ECONOMY
description: Global economic interdependence has traditionally been regarded as a major source of efficiency, productivity growth, investment, and technological progress. However, geopolitical tensions, concentrated supply chains, financial vulnerabilities, and disruptions to international trade have increasingly challenged the assumption that deeper integration automatically produces greater economic security. This article examines how countries can preserve the developmental benefits of international economic integration while reducing the strategic vulnerabilities associated with excessive dependence. Using a conceptual and comparative analytical approach, the study synthesizes recent research on geoeconomic fragmentation, supply-chain resilience, and long-term economic development. It argues that resilience should not be equated with economic self-sufficiency or the indiscriminate relocation of production. Instead, resilience depends on the quality of economic interdependence, the availability of credible alternatives, domestic productive capabilities, institutional adaptability, and the capacity to respond to external shocks without sacrificing long-term competitiveness. The article proposes the Strategic Interdependence and Development Resilience Framework (SIDRF) , a multidimensional framework for evaluating economic dependencies and integrating resilience into national development planning. The framework distinguishes productive interdependence from critical vulnerability and identifies four strategic dimensions: dependency exposure, adaptive capacity, productive transformation, and institutional coordination. The article concludes that sustainable development requires selective diversification, capability-building, and international cooperation rather than generalized economic decoupling. The proposed framework offers a basis for future empirical research and strategic policy design. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23532218

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF DIGITAL MANAGEMENT TECHNOLOGIES AND ASSESSMENT OF THEIR EFFECTIVENESS IN SERVICE ENTERPRISES

The features, trends and ways of further development of management services, the current state and global trends of the digital economy were analyzed, and measures for its further development in Uzbekistan were proposed. The article also reviewed research on innovative infrastructure facilities for managing innovative ecosystem services. Also, proposals and recommendations for the digitalization of the service sector were developed. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23245819

title: IMPROVING CUSTOMER-CENTRIC MANAGEMENT IN COMMERCIAL BANKS
description: This paper develops scientific and methodological foundations and practical recommendations for improving customer-centric management in commercial banks. Economic and statistical analysis, comparative analysis, a systems approach and expert assessment were used. The findings substantiate the need for deeper customer segmentation, service personalization and new service models based on digital technologies and artificial intelligence. Recommendations address the effectiveness of customer relationship management (CRM) systems, continuous staff development and a customer-centric corporate culture. The proposed measures serve to strengthen customer loyalty, improve service quality and expand banks' market share. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23275323

title: IMPROVING THE ASSESSMENT OF CORPORATE FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE AND INVESTMENT DECISION-MAKING IN THE CONTEXT OF TAX ADMINISTRATION DIGITALIZATION
description: This article examines the theoretical and practical aspects of assessing corporate financial performance and improving investment decision-making in the context of tax administration digitalization. It explores the role of electronic tax reporting, digital data exchange, and automated analytical tools in enhancing the accuracy, transparency, and timeliness of information regarding corporate financial activities. The study also considers the opportunities for evaluating corporate liquidity, solvency, financial stability, and profitability through the effective use of data generated by digital tax administration systems. Particular attention is given to the comprehensive analysis of financial indicators, the evaluation of investment project efficiency, the assessment of financial risks, and the rational allocation of investment resources. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23527677

title: IMPROVING THE FUNCTIONING OF THE INNOVATION ECONOMY
description: This article examines institutional and economic mechanisms for improving the functioning of the innovation economy, with particular attention to the interaction among research institutions, enterprises, government agencies, and financial organizations. The study aims to identify barriers to the transformation of knowledge into commercially viable technologies, products, and services. It adopts a qualitative framework combining a literature review, institutional analysis, and comparative assessment of innovation support mechanisms. The discussion focuses on research financing, technology transfer, human capital development, intellectual property management, and university–industry cooperation. Particular attention is given to the relevance of these mechanisms for developing economies, including Uzbekistan. The article develops an analytical framework linking innovation inputs, institutional coordination, commercialization processes, and economic outcomes. It proposes measures to improve policy coherence, strengthen enterprise participation in innovation, and evaluate support programmes through measurable results. The framework provides a basis for further empirical investigation of national innovation performance. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23489401

title: INSTITUTIONAL AND LEGAL FOUNDATIONS OF THE FORMATION AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE VALUE ADDED TAX SYSTEM IN THE REPUBLIC OF UZBEKISTAN
description: This article examines the formation and development of the value added tax (VAT) system in Uzbekistan from the early transition years to the present. Using doctrinal legal analysis, historical-comparative and institutional approaches, it traces how the legal framework moved from fragmented regulation to a codified system and identifies the institutional drivers of reform. The study finds that the evolution of VAT in Uzbekistan has followed three directions: codification and unification of rules, gradual rate and base rationalization, and digitalization of administration. It also identifies persisting challenges, including refund delays, tax gaps, and the frequency of legislative change. The article concludes with policy recommendations for strengthening legal certainty and administrative efficiency. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23232448
tags: ["value added tax, Uzbekistan, Tax Code, tax reform, institutional framework, tax administration, digital economy"]

title: INVESTMENT ATTRACTIVENESS AND ECONOMIC SECURITY IN UZBEKISTAN: INSTITUTIONAL DETERMINANTS AND STRATEGIC CHALLENGES
description: Uzbekistan has made foreign capital a central goal of its economic strategy, but more investment does not automatically mean a safer economy. This article looks at two questions: how institutional quality is related to foreign direct investment (FDI), and whether the country's growing appeal to investors has come with new external vulnerabilities. I use public data on investment, governance and the external balance, and apply trend comparison, regression analysis and a simple vulnerability index. Better governance, regulatory quality above all, goes together with higher FDI, though this is a long-run co-movement and cannot be read as proven causation. Over the same years, reliance on external debt and remittances has also grown. The article proposes stronger contract enforcement, a broader investment base and closer management of external liabilities. In my view, the harder task now is making that capital durable. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23587803
tags: ["foreign direct investment, institutional quality, economic security, Uzbekistan, external vulnerability"]

title: Instrument-level coding of US financial sanctions against Russia (2014–2025) and China (2018–2026)
description: Instrument-level coding of US financial sanctions against Russia (2014–2025) and China (2018–2026) This dataset records the author's instrument-level coding of 21 US sanctions instruments deployed against Russia (n = 9, 2014–2024) and China (n = 12, 2018–2025), underlying the article "The Self-Limiting Hegemon: Competitive Financial Interdependence and the Limits of US Financial Statecraft" (Review of International Political Economy, submitted). Each instrument is coded along three design features: - Scope: binary, comprehensive (economy-wide) vs. targeted (sector-, entity-, or product-specific). - Calibration: ordinal, recording the presence of phase-ins, exemptions, waivers, carve-outs, and licensing. - Reversibility: ordinal, measuring the economic disruption caused by withdrawal (not legal revocability); low reversibility closes a channel the target's economy depends on. The dataset also flags boundary cases (R8 oil price cap; C11–C12 2025 tariff escalation) that move beyond the targeted pole but are reversed within a short window. All source documents are publicly available (OFAC actions, BIS rules, Federal Register notices, US Treasury statements and testimony). Intercoder reliability: scope κ = 1.00, calibration κ = 0.93, reversibility κ = 0.40 (re-examined under a stricter robustness threshold; four Russian and zero Chinese instruments survive). Columns: ID, Case, Year, Instrument, Scope, Calibration, Reversibility. Cite as: Yuhong Li, "Instrument-level coding of US financial sanctions against Russia (2014–2025) and China (2018–2026)," 10.5281/zenodo.23407651. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23407651

title: METHODS FOR DETERMINING IONIZING RADIATION DOSE RATE AND ITS HYGIENIC ASSESSMENT
description: Ionizing radiation sources are widely used in medicine, industry, scientific research, and other fields. However, the biological effects of ionizing radiation depend on its type, energy, absorbed dose, dose rate, and duration of exposure. Therefore, proper dosimetric monitoring and accurate determination of dose rate are important components of radiation safety. This article describes the concept of ionizing radiation dose rate, the main dosimetric methods used for its determination, the instruments applied for measurements, and the basic principles for hygienic assessment of the obtained results. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23239097

title: Metagenomic and transcriptomic analyses of tomato rhizosphere and leaves treated with a biowaste-derived extract
description: PERCIVAL (Processi di EstRazione di bioprodotti da sCarti agroIndustriali e VALorizzazione in cascata) project (PON  ARS01_00869) focuses on the development and optimization of innovative processes for the valorization of agro-industrial residues using a cascade biorefinery approach. The project aims to maximize resource efficiency by enabling the sequential recovery of high-value products from heterogeneous biomass streams. The targeted outputs include bioactive compounds (e.g. antioxidants and polyphenols), chemical building blocks (e.g. lactic acid), and advanced materials (e.g. nutraceutical ingredients, high-performance fibers, and bioplastics such as PLA). Residual fractions generated along the processing chain are further exploited for the production of biofuels (e.g. biomethane) and agricultural inputs (e.g. soil amendments, biochar, and biostimulants). Biological and molecular data generated within the project support the characterization, screening, and optimization of bioprocesses and feedstocks. The project also includes the assessment of environmental and economic sustainability of the proposed value chains, considering the entire lifecycle from raw material sourcing to final product generation. The data provided in this repository relate to a controlled-condition experiment on pot-grown tomato plants ( Solanum lycopersicum cv. Moneymaker). Plants were treated weekly with two different doses of a biowaste-based extract. To assess the efficacy and impact of this treatment, a multi-disciplinary approach was applied, encompassing:  Rhizosphere eDNA metabarcoding (16S and ITS)  Plant transcriptomics (RNA-Seq)  Plant physiological phenotyping  Soil and leaf chemical analyses The raw omics sequencing reads associated with this study have been deposited at the NCBI Sequence Read Archive (SRA) under BioProject PRJNA1425279. title: Mystery in the Midden: Deciphering the Function of Whittled Sticks
description: Abstract In this paper we investigate the function of whittled wooden sticks found in medieval Norwegian urban contexts, commonly known as 'sausage pegs'. While traditionally interpreted as tools for sealing sausages, comparative finds from other northern European countries suggest multiple possible uses, including their deployment in the medieval wool trade as bale pins. This study employs a two-proxy chemical approach: gas chromatography–high resolution mass spectrometry (GC-HRMS) to detect and quantify lipid organic residues, and liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to identify proteins absorbed in the wood. GC-HRMS analysis reveals a convergent assemblage of animal sterols (cholesterol, lathosterol), even- and odd-chain fatty acids, diterpenic markers of heat treatment, and fruit-derived acids. Proteomic analysis independently identifies ruminant blood proteins and cartilage/muscle tissue markers in four of the five samples. The combined dataset provides multi-proxy evidence for contact with ruminant meat and blood products, supporting the sausage peg hypothesis for the Oslo assemblage while acknowledging residual uncertainties. Comparative analysis with similar artefacts from England and Denmark, and reference data from uncontaminated archaeological wood, contextualises the chemical findings. The study proposes the term 'closing pin' to encompass the multifunctional nature of these artefacts. title: PROMOTING GREEN CONSUMPTION AND ENVIRONMENTALLY RESPONSIBLE ECONOMIC DECISIONS THROUGH BEHAVIORAL ECONOMICS: STATISTICAL EVIDENCE AND POLICY SCENARIOS FROM UZBEKISTAN
description: The transition toward a green and circular economy requires not only technological modernization and institutional reforms but also fundamental changes in consumer behavior. This article examines the potential contribution of behavioral economics to promoting environmentally responsible consumption and improving waste management outcomes in Uzbekistan. The study integrates concepts of bounded rationality, social norms, loss aversion, default effects, and behavioral nudging with descriptive statistical analysis based on official government publications. According to the Agency for Waste Management and Circular Economy Development, Uzbekistan generated approximately 14.8 million tonnes of household waste in 2024 and 15.1 million tonnes in 2025. An official report on 2024 activities indicates that 766.3 thousand tonnes of household waste were recycled, equivalent to approximately 5.2% of generated waste. Another government publication reports a broader processing figure of more than 900.5 thousand tonnes, highlighting the importance of statistical definitions. The study calculates an annual waste-generation growth rate of approximately 2.03%, analyzes service coverage and waste management indicators, and develops hypothetical scenarios for improving material recovery through behavioral interventions. Under a scenario in which recovery reaches 15% of the 2025 waste-generation baseline, the amount of recovered material would equal approximately 2.265 million tonnes. This estimate is a scenario rather than a forecast. The findings suggest that well-designed behavioral interventions may complement infrastructure investment, environmental education, and regulatory reforms. The article proposes a framework integrating household waste separation, information feedback, social norms, economic incentives, and measurable environmental outcomes. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23597505

title: PUBLIC DEBT AND ECONOMIC GROWTH: DOES THE COMPOSITION OF GOVERNMENT BORROWING MATTER MORE THAN ITS SIZE?
description: Public debt is often discussed as if its size alone determines whether it helps or harms an economy. This article argues that the purpose, productivity and financing conditions of borrowing are equally important. Debt used for well-selected infrastructure, education, health and research can raise productivity and future tax revenues; borrowing that mainly supports recurring expenditure without lasting economic benefits can leave future taxpayers with repayment obligations but few new resources. However, even productive projects can become harmful when they are poorly planned, overpriced, delayed or financed at unsustainable interest rates. Drawing on international research and proposing a country-panel research design, the article explains the channels linking debt, public investment and real GDP per capita growth. It concludes that governments should assess both debt sustainability and the quality of spending, rather than rely on a single debt-to-GDP threshold. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23475096

title: REGULATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN THE FIELD OF COPYRIGHT: THE EUROPEAN UNION EXPERIENCE AND PROSPECTS FOR IMPROVING UZBEKISTAN'S LEGISLATION
description: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies has raised significant theoretical and practical challenges for copyright regulation. This article examines the legal framework governing the interaction between AI and copyright in the European Union (EU), with a view to identifying approaches that may inform the further development of Uzbekistan’s legislation. Particular attention is paid to Directive (EU) 2019/790 on copyright and related rights in the Digital Single Market, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (the AI Act), and the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice. The study analyses the use of copyright-protected works for AI model training, the legal framework for text and data mining (TDM), the protection of rightsholders’ interests, transparency requirements concerning training data, and the copyright status of AI-generated content. Using formal legal analysis, comparative legal analysis, systematic analysis, and legal interpretation, the article identifies the principal features and limitations of the EU approach. It argues that an effective regulatory framework should balance technological innovation with the protection of authors’ and other rightsholders’ legitimate interests. On this basis, the article proposes measures to improve Uzbekistan’s legislation, including clarifying the legal status of AI-assisted and AI-generated works, establishing differentiated rules for TDM, developing mechanisms for rights reservations and licensing, strengthening transparency obligations for relevant AI model providers, and improving procedures for handling copyright complaints and disputes. The article concludes that a gradual, context-sensitive approach could help Uzbekistan develop a balanced legal framework for AI and copyright. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23507197
tags: ["artificial intelligence; copyright; generative AI; European Union; AI Act; Digital Single Market Directive; text and data mining; training data; rightsholders; digital economy."]

title: STRATEGIC AUTONOMY WITHOUT ISOLATION: A NEW PARADIGM FOR NATIONAL DEVELOPMENT IN AN ERA OF GEOECONOMIC FRAGMENTATION
description: The changing structure of the global economy presents national policymakers with a strategic dilemma: how can countries preserve access to international markets, investment, and technology while maintaining the capacity to make independent economic decisions under conditions of geopolitical uncertainty? This article conceptualizes strategic autonomy as a development capability rather than a condition of economic self-sufficiency. Drawing on recent research published between 2024 and 2026 by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD), the World Bank, and the World Trade Organization (WTO), the study examines the relationships between geoeconomic fragmentation, investment concentration, technological dependence, productive transformation, and national development. The analysis develops the Strategic Autonomy without Isolation Framework (SAIF) , a conceptual model organized around five dimensions: strategic exposure, economic option capacity, domestic capability formation, institutional adaptability, and international network positioning. The framework distinguishes formal economic independence from the substantive ability to substitute suppliers, redirect trade, maintain access to essential technologies, and transform international investment into domestic productive capabilities. The article further develops four propositions concerning the relationship between diversification, technological learning, institutional quality, and resilience-adjusted competitiveness. Its central argument is that neither unrestricted dependence nor generalized economic decoupling provides an adequate foundation for long-term development. Instead, sustainable strategic autonomy requires selective risk management, productive investment, credible economic alternatives, and institutional coordination. The framework offers a theoretical foundation for future empirical research and policy design, particularly in developing economies seeking to improve their position within changing global value chains. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23543339

title: Simulation Results for High-Resolution PV-BESS Operation and Energy Sharing: A Latvian Case Study
description: This dataset contains simulation outputs supporting the study "A High-Resolution Decision-Support Framework for PV-BESS Operation and Energy Sharing". The dataset covers single-property and two-property active-customer configurations, photovoltaic generation, battery energy storage operation under self-consumption and price-arbitrage strategies, virtual monetary settlement, and electricity sharing within energy communities. title: Source Data for Josephson et al.: The Economics of Climate Adaptation: A Bounded Narrative Review of Methodologies
description: This dataset contains the source-level coding record for The Economics of Climate Adaptation: A Bounded Narrative Review of Methodologies . It covers 85 sources identified through purposive selection of 14 foundational documents, backward and forward citation tracing, and a targeted literature update covering 2023 through 2025. The Excel file records each source’s corpus route, publication type, primary method and evidence orientation, sector, geography and scale, income context, and principal estimand and counterfactual. It provides the classifications underlying the manuscript’s summary characterization of the reviewed literature. The corpus reflects a bounded, structured narrative review rather than an exhaustive systematic search. Classifications describe the identified sources and should not be interpreted as estimates of the prevalence of methods or evidence types across the wider adaptation literature. title: Supplementary Information: Techno-economic and environmental investigation of Power-to-X at various greenfield and brownfield levels - a structured multi-level infrastructure access framework for PtX
description: Description: This dataset contains the complete input parameters, life cycle inventory (LCI) data, and simulation results underlying the techno-economic and life cycle assessment (LCA) presented in "Techno-economic and environmental investigation of Power-to-X at various greenfield and brownfield levels - a structured multi-level infrastructure access framework for PtX". title: Suspect list of persistent, mobile and toxic (PMT), and very persistent and very mobile (vPvM) chemicals, with predicted collision-cross section (SSC) values developed in the frame of the NePMTune project
description: This list was prepared within the NePMTune Project (Towards water circular economy protection from the threat caused by persistent, mobile and toxic chemicals) funded by Agencia Estatal de Investigación MCIN/AEI/10.13039/501100011033 and the European Union through NextGeneration/PRTR funds (refs. TED2021-129200B-C41, TED2021-129200B-C42). More information will be provided in an upcoming publication, with the following tentative title: Tracking persistent and mobile chemicals across the urban water cycle.   This suspect list of persistent, mobile and toxic (PMT), or very persistent and very mobile (vPvM) chemicals (in brief PMs) was prepared as from multiple data sources, as follows: 1)      A list of approximately 1000 substances, which were either previously classified by (Montes et al., 2022) under the former PM criteria or detected in surface water or wastewater (Montes et al., 2022). 2)      The German Environmental Agency (UBA) UBAPMT | Prioritized PMT/vPvM substances in the REACH registration database (Arp et al., 2023a). 3)      The PMT/vPvM assessment of REACH registered Substances Detected in Wastewater Treatment Plant Effluent, Freshwater Resources and Drinking Water report from UBA (Arp et al., 2023b). 4)      Two relevant publications containing PMT monitoring data published in 2021: a study from China by (Huang et al., 2021) and another from Germany by (Neuwald et al., 2021). After removing duplicates, the final compiled list comprised 1889 unique compounds. All these substances were submitted to PMT/vPvM classification by applying the European Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/707 (European Commission, 2023) (CLP regulation) as described below. Although the CLP regulation establishes the mobility criteria based on log K oc values, this study utilizes log D values for simplicity, maintaining consistency with the previous work of (Montes et al., 2022). The cut-off for mobile compounds was set at log D = 3.5, while the very mobile category was set at log D = 2.5. For the remaining criteria, regarding persistence and toxicity were previously described by (Montes et al., 2022) Briefly, a substance was considered to be very persistent (vP) if the biological oxygen demand (BOD) was equal to or less than 30% and persistent (P) if the BOD was between 30 and 40% and the probability of biodegradation was less than 0.5 (experimental data and BIOWIN 5 and 6 models). A substance was considered to be toxic (T) if the lowest long-term non-observed effect concentration (NOEC) for marine or freshwater organisms was less than 0.01 mg L -1 , the LC50 was less than 1 mg L -1 , or the substance met the criteria for classification as carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic for reproduction. Moreover, those compounds classified as Cramer class III were considered to be potentially toxic (Pot T). The above-mentioned criteria have previously been applied both in the report “Prioritised PMT/vPvM substances in the REACH registration database” published by UBA (Arp et al., 2023a) and by (Huang et al., 2021). Consequently, the information found in those sources and the final classification were transferred to the present work. For the compounds prioritized by (Montes et al., 2022), a reclassification was performed using the new mobility criteria indicated above. For compounds derived from the UBA report (Arp et al., 2023a,b) and the monitoring study of (Neuwald et al., 2021), a search was conducted for properties related to persistence, mobility and toxicity. These compounds were then evaluated using the PMT criteria described above, following the methodology detailed by (Montes et al., 2022). title: System Usability Scale (SUS) Dataset for Dual-Interface Used Cooking Oil Management Application
description: This dataset contains the raw System Usability Scale (SUS) questionnaire responses and score calculations used to evaluate the perceived usability of the user interface (UI/UX) of a proposed used cooking oil management application in Surabaya, Indonesia. The study assesses a dual-interface design tailored to two distinct user segments: stationary depositors (households and food-and-beverage businesses) and mobile field collectors. The dataset comprises responses from 19 participants: 14 depositors and 5 field collectors. It includes the raw 5-point Likert responses for all 10 SUS items, the step-by-step score conversion matrix, the final SUS score per respondent, and summary statistics per group. The mean SUS scores are 74 for depositors (Acceptable) and 69 for collectors (Marginal). The data serve as the quantitative usability evaluation of a digital prototype developed using the Design Thinking methodology. The questionnaire was administered in Indonesian, and English translations of the statements are provided in the Codebook sheet. Data were collected in July-August 2026. All data are anonymized and contain no personally identifiable information. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22812162

title: TECHNOLOGICAL PROCESSES OF ORGANIC SYNTHESIS: PROCESS-LEVEL STRUCTURE, GREEN METRICS AND ENABLING TECHNOLOGIES
description: This article examines the technological processes of organic synthesis as an integrated system of chemical transformation, separation, purification and waste-management operations rather than as a single reaction step. The aim is to identify, on the basis of published evidence and transparent calculations, the technological decisions that most strongly determine the material efficiency, safety and scalability of organic synthesis. A structured analytical review of peer-reviewed literature (1991–2023) was combined with quantitative evaluation of atom economy for representative reaction types and with a comparative analysis of two industrial case studies: the manufacture of ibuprofen (Boots and BHC routes) and of sitagliptin (rhodium-catalysed asymmetric hydrogenation versus transaminase biocatalysis). The calculations show that atom economy ranges from 100% for addition reactions such as the Diels–Alder reaction and catalytic hydrogenation to 25.7% for the Wittig methylenation of cyclohexanone, and that the change from a stoichiometric six-step route to a catalytic three-step route raises the atom economy of ibuprofen synthesis from about 40% to 77.5%. Published data further indicate that solvents account for the largest share of process mass in fine-chemical and pharmaceutical manufacture, and that continuous-flow, microwave-assisted and biocatalytic technologies improve heat transfer, selectivity or safety under defined conditions. A five-stage decision framework for designing technological processes of organic synthesis is proposed. The results can be used in process development and in teaching organic technology. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23533436

title: THE EVOLUTION OF ECONOMIC THOUGHT ON SERVICES AND VALUE CREATION
description: This article reviews how economic thought, from classical political economy to modern service research, has understood the role of services in creating wealth and value. The approaches are compared by what they count as productive activity, what they analyze (a sector, a firm, or a market), and how they explain value creation through services. Five positions are identified: early views linking productive activity to agriculture or material accumulation; Marx’s concept of surplus value; the neoclassical view based on utility and market exchange; theories of structural change and the knowledge economy; and modern approaches in which value is created through service provision, use, and interaction. These positions overlap rather than form stages that every economy must pass through, and the article also separates the growth of the service sector from the servitization of firms and from service-dominant logic. It concludes that modern approaches widen the study of services without removing sectoral differences or the importance of material production, while the proposed matrix helps compare theories with different meanings of value and productivity. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23239734

title: THE IMPACT OF BEHAVIORAL ECONOMICS ON FINANCIAL DECISION-MAKING AND SAVING BEHAVIOR IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY: EMPIRICAL TRENDS AND POLICY IMPLICATIONS FROM UZBEKISTAN
description: The rapid expansion of digital financial services has transformed how individuals manage income, make payments, save money, and respond to financial incentives. This study examines the relationship between digital financial development and household financial behavior in Uzbekistan through the theoretical framework of behavioral economics. Particular attention is paid to present bias, mental accounting, financial self-control, loss aversion, and choice architecture. The research employs descriptive statistical analysis, comparative assessment, growth-rate calculations, structural ratio analysis, and scenario modeling based on official data published by the Central Bank of Uzbekistan. The findings indicate that funds credited to bank cards increased from UZS 789 trillion in 2023 to UZS 1,496 trillion in 2025, representing cumulative growth of approximately 89.6%. Meanwhile, the ratio of cash withdrawals to funds credited to bank cards declined from approximately 24.0% to 18.6%. Total banking system deposits increased from UZS 308.7 trillion at the beginning of 2025 to UZS 417.3 trillion at the beginning of 2026. These developments demonstrate significant changes in the financial environment in which consumers make payment and saving decisions. However, aggregate financial indicators do not establish whether digital financial services directly improve self-control or household saving behavior. The study develops a behavioral-financial framework and proposes digital interventions including automated saving options, expenditure feedback, financial goal-setting, and transparent choice architecture. The proposed measures aim to strengthen financial resilience and improve the quality of household financial decision-making. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23596957

title: TIMBER: A Trade-Instruction Multimodal Benchmark for Evidence Retrieval in German-Language Video Question Answering
description: TIMBER is a German-language multimodal video question answering benchmark for the skilled trades, built from publicly available instructional videos on YouTube. It comprises 155 videos (~27 hours) across 15 activity fields, with 310 question–answer pairs phrased in the register of an apprentice, each grounded in its source video by a temporal evidence span. Each question carries three labels: question type, required modality, and knowledge accessibility (explicit / derivable / implicit), the analytical core of the benchmark. The corpus additionally carries a manually produced segment-level annotation layer of 1,300 action segments with objects and on-screen text as oriented bounding boxes. Copyright note: This record contains only annotations and pointers (video IDs and timestamps) to the public source videos. No video, audio, frames, or transcripts are redistributed. The CC BY 4.0 licence covers only the annotations and codebook. The source videos remain subject to YouTube's terms and their creators' rights. Contents: timber_qa_catalog.csv - 310 QA pairs with labels and evidence spans, and the external answer source for implicit items timber_video_metadata.csv - metadata for all 155 videos timber_annotations.zip - 155 segment-level annotation files (JSON) codebook.md, README.md, LICENSE.txt The benchmark is intended for evaluation rather than training. It is described in the paper "TIMBER: A Trade-Instruction Multimodal Benchmark for Evidence Retrieval in German-Language Video Question Answering", KEEPER 2026 Workshop, co-located with ACM CIKM 2026, Rome, Italy (CEUR Workshop Proceedings, to appear). title: The China Discount Revisited: Sector Structure, State Ownership and the Valuation Gap between the Largest US and Chinese Listed Firms
description: Rising geopolitical rivalry between the United States and China has renewed interest in whether investors systematically value Chinese companies below comparable American ones, the so-called “China discount”. This paper tests the size and sources of the discount using a hand-assembled cross-section of the 100 largest listed companies in each country by market capitalisation, with trailing-twelve-month earnings and revenue retrieved in October 2026. The median price-to-earnings ratio is 9.1 for Chinese firms and 18.3 for US firms; the aggregate ratio is 9.0 versus 20.5. Earnings margins are statistically indistinguishable (median 22.3% versus 23.1%). A decomposition shows that 45% of the aggregate gap reflects sector composition, since Chinese market value is concentrated in banks and energy and US value in technology; the remaining 55% reflects lower valuations within the same sectors. Controlling for sector, size and profitability, Chinese firms trade at P/E ratios about 49.5% lower (p < 0.001). Two further results qualify common narratives. First, state ownership carries no significant discount once sector and size are held constant: the raw SOE discount is a composition effect. Second, the discount is concentrated outside technology. Chinese technology firms trade at 23.6% below US peers (not significant), against 50.6% in other sectors (interaction p = 0.016). The findings are consistent with a country-level institutional and geopolitical risk premium that investors waive in strategically favoured sectors. We discuss implications for multinational strategy, portfolio allocation and emerging-market policymakers. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23657635

title: Transforming Tacit Knowledge into Explicit Knowledge through Digital Repository Implementation to Prevent the Loss of Corporate Intellectual Assets
description: Organizations in the knowledge-based economy are exposed to the loss of intellectual assets whenever experienced employees depart before their tacit knowledge has been documented. This study examines how digital repository implementation supports the transformation of tacit knowledge into explicit knowledge and the preservation of intellectual assets, with a knowledge sharing culture acting as the social enabler. Grounded in knowledge management system theory and the SECI model, a quantitative explanatory survey was administered to 189 employees of knowledge-based organizations that use digital repositories, and the data were analyzed with PLS-SEM using SmartPLS. The measurement model met the criteria for convergent validity, construct reliability, and discriminant validity. The model accounted for 52.7% of the variance in knowledge transformation and 66.2% in intellectual asset preservation. Every direct structural path was positive and statistically significant: digital repository implementation was related to knowledge transformation (β = 0.299) and to intellectual asset preservation (β = 0.483), and knowledge transformation was related to intellectual asset preservation (β = 0.424). Knowledge sharing culture showed the strongest relationship with knowledge transformation (β = 0.547), but it did not significantly moderate the relationship between digital repository implementation and knowledge transformation (β = 0.056, p = 0.325). These results suggest that technological infrastructure and organizational knowledge-sharing practices both matter for transforming and preserving organizational knowledge. The study offers an integrated socio-technical model linking technology, culture, knowledge conversion, and asset preservation. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23335093

title: USING CIRCULAR ECONOMY STRATEGIES TO ENHANCE COMPANY COMPETITIVENESS
description: The article analyzes the application of circular economy strategies as a primary mechanism for maintaining and enhancing company competitiveness in modern markets. Moving away from the traditional "take-make-dispose" linear model, four core circular strategies are examined: resource recovery, product life extension, sharing platforms, and product-as-a-service models. The study evaluates how these models directly influence competitive advantage through cost reduction, innovation, regulatory resilience, and enhanced brand equity. The article concludes with an assessment of how transition economies can implement these strategies and provides practical recommendations for corporate leaders seeking long-term sustainability. title: Water Governance Perceptions in the Santa Ana River Watershed, California: Survey Data and Questionnaire
description: This dataset contains survey materials and responses collected to assess institutional stakeholder perceptions of water governance in the Santa Ana River Watershed (SARW), southern California, USA. The assessment was conducted using the Governance and Stakeholders component of the Freshwater Health Index (FHI). The survey was administered between February 2024 and January 2025 to 35 professionals involved in water resources management, environmental regulation, planning, research, consulting, and ecological conservation. The questionnaire consists of 51 perception-based questions organized into 12 governance sub-indicators and four major indicators: Enabling Environment, Stakeholder Engagement, Effectiveness, and Vision and Adaptive Governance. The supporting Excel workbook contains question-level survey responses, skipped responses, question-level descriptive statistics, and calculated respondent-level governance scores. The accompanying PDF includes the informed consent statement and complete survey questionnaire. These materials support research examining variation in governance perceptions across management dimensions and geographic areas of the SARW. The data were previously included in the supplementary materials accompanying the doctoral dissertation of Qin (2026), University of California, Riverside. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23484751

title: Who Breaks the News? Measuring Concentration, Latency, and Diffusion Structure in Uzbekistan's Telegram News Ecosystem
description: Telegram is the main news infrastructure in Uzbekistan, a country of 37 million people with an estimated 25 million Telegram users. Because the platform makes republication effortless and attribution optional, a few newsrooms may supply the stories that hundreds of channels redistribute. This paper asks how centralised the flow of information in this ecosystem is and examines three dimensions: concentration, latency and diffusion structure. It combines two sources of real data. The first is a cross-section of the 100 largest Uzbek news channels in the TGStat catalogue, covering subscribers, average post reach and the citation index, a measure of how often a channel is cited and reposted by other channels. The second is a manual trace of 25 story families (55 posts) identified in the public web previews of 15 leading channels (264 posts). Citations are markedly more concentrated than audiences: the Gini coefficient is 0.61 for the citation index against 0.46 for subscribers, and the bottom half of channels receives only 8.2% of citations but holds 19.8% of subscribers. Concentration is nonetheless moderate in absolute terms (CR₁₀ = 38.9%, HHI = 259), and the largest channel by subscribers ranks only 48th by citations. In the traced families, the first republication followed the root after a median of 20 minutes (all republications: median 38 minutes, IQR 10–124). None of the 264 posts was a native forward of another news channel, so republication took place entirely through unattributed copying. Rather than a single-hub star, the observed structure is one of reciprocal copying among peer channels, with official sources feeding professional media. Root posts reached a larger share of their channel's audience than copies in 64% of families (Wilcoxon p = 0.06). We discuss the implications for the economics of originality and for attribution norms, and outline an embedding-based pipeline for scaling the analysis. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23525620

title: Wind Fragility Database for Electrical Power Infrastructure
description: A database of 507 published wind fragility curves for electrical power infrastructure, collected from 52 sources published between 2008 and 2026: transmission towers, steel transmission monopoles, wood, steel and concrete distribution poles, conductors, ground wires, insulators, overhead line systems and substations. Each curve records its source and the figure or table it came from, its functional form and parameters, and how its source defines the wind speed (averaging time, reference height and terrain exposure), so that users can judge which curves can be compared. The record includes a user guide, an Excel workbook and CSV tables of the data, and a MATLAB interface that evaluates every curve, including the parametric fragility functions of steel transmission monopoles from the companion preprints (Parts I and II). It was produced for the Atlantic Marine Energy Center (AMEC).  DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23399966
